entry.title: I built BoardEject: an open-source Apple Freeform Excalidraw converter
entry.summary:
I wanted a way to get editable content out of Apple Freeform instead of only ending up with a flattened PDF. So I built BoardEject. The basic flow is: Freeform → BoardEject → editable .excalidraw Where supported, BoardEject preserves things like: shapes text connectors groups drawings tables images
Unsupported or unverified structures are reported instead of silently pretending the conversion worked. The interesting part has been validating behavior against real macOS Freeform captures rather than only synthetic fixtures. It’s local-first, open source, and the board content isn’t uploaded to a server. Try it: https://boardeject.dev Source: https://github.com/royalpinto007/boardeject I’m still working through native edge cases, so feedback from people who use Freeform or Excalidraw heavily would be useful.

entry.title: Context aware Spring AI chat microservice
entry.summary:
Keeping State in a Stateless World: Building a Context-Aware Gemini Microservice with Spring AI and H2
By default, Large Language Models (LLMs) are completely stateless. Every API call you make to Google Gemini is treated like a first-time introduction. If a user says "My name is Alex" in request one, and "What is my name?" in request two, Gemini will not know the answer. To build a true chatbot experience, your microservice needs to remember the conversation history. In this post, we will build a Spring Boot microservice that connects to the Gemini API, uses Spring AI's ChatMemory Advisor to maintain context, and backs up that history using a persistent H2 database mapped to unique user sessions. entry.title: Measure the Tool-Loop Tax Before You Ship Work Off the Laptop
entry.summary: On a Thursday evening a backend engineer closed a laptop that still held one unfinished agent session. The session had been rewriting a Flyway migration that referenced a staging password kept inside a local dotenv file. Office Wi-Fi had already dropped twice, and each reconnect added seconds to every remote tool call in the loop. The engineer needed a placement rule that treated latency, secret residency, and offline survival as measured inputs rather than slogans. Agent loops look inexpensive in screenshots because those screenshots omit the network path under every tool call. Each departing tool call pays a round-trip tax, and that tax multiplies by retrieve-edit-test cycles inside a single job. entry.summary: The request I hear most often this year sounds the same every time: "We want a bot that answers from our documents and does not make things up." The technical name is RAG, retrieval-augmented generation. Below, without jargon: what it is, who it pays off for, what your company needs to bring, and where these projects break. entry.title: The Budget Card Workshop
entry.summary: A lab room at 3:40 p.m. still had one process running. The previous session had asked a coding assistant for a robust HTTP client with retries, then pointed that client at a tiny charging endpoint that failed on purpose. Students packed laptops while the terminal kept printing the same line, like a metronome that refused to leave the stage. That scene is the whole workshop. AI-generated clients often sound careful.
